theme: Learned sign classes, conditional-length grammar prediction and compositional field hypotheses
question: Can the stochastic grammar recommendation be carried into learned class productions with grouped held-out prediction, and can those classes improve matched sign-level backoff?
outcome: On 1596 unique texts and 8009 tokens, the primary class grammar loses 0.472591 bits/token against tuned Markov and gains 0.291203 over position. The exploratory Markov-plus-class mixture gains 0.055708 bits/token over the equally tuned Markov-plus-position mixture, with conditional component-bootstrap interval [0.043647,0.067463]. Six synthetic controls show grammar gains under invented administrative and compositional accounts; an exact semantic twin has likelihood ratio 1. Learned class/production inventory, late-attachment hypotheses and frozen next-data predictions are retained.
challenge: Full-register object/string closure yields a 180-text component and token-weight effective component count 123.1. Grammar classes are only partly stable; all primary folds select the largest state count. UNKNOWN events collapse distinct unseen graphics, and the class model has poor unknown-bucket calibration. Generic HMM induction already has Tiwari2026 precedent. Backoff families were designed after exposed outer outcomes.
remedy: Preserved run-v1, wrote separate post-outcome protocols and runs-v2/v3, matched mixture grids/alphabets, verified normalization/forward scores/closure and independent positional mixture arithmetic, retained source priors and synthetic identifiability witness, and froze a later-object prediction recipe.
retry_when: A source-checked genuinely excluded/new object population permits evaluation of the frozen class and position backoff recipes. Semantic scenarios require independent object-use, issuing-group or contents joins. A revised grammar/UNKNOWN calibration requires a new protocol and output, preserving current failures.
